messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: P2 continuous-batching throughput cliff + kv cache churn detected in eu-west-1. Alert: requests 5xx up 18%, token latency p95 up 2.1s. Auto-escalate to oncall.

olivia: taking it, jumping in. oncall here.

raj: quick snapshot: eviction_rate spiked 8x at 09:12, kv_cache_miss_ratio up to 0.67, avg_microbatch_size jumped from 2 -> 11 for reader-service. Looks like prefetch window overshot and batches coalesced.

chen: I can roll a hotfix to clamp microbatch size & reduce prefetch window. Suggest steps: set continuous_batch.max_microbatch=4 and prefetch.window_ms=40, enable short-circuit throttle for noisy routes.

olivia: agree. What's the safest deploy path? canary 10% then monitor.

chen: plan — create a feature-flagged config and canary via control plane:
```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/configs 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' 
  -d '{"service":"continuous-batcher","config":{"max_microbatch":4,"prefetch_window_ms":40},"canary":0.1}'
```

raj: also gonna temporarily rate-limit the top noisy route (route=/v1/generate, customer=heavy-client) to 5rps to reduce KV pressure.

olivia: do it and restart batcher pods after config flips.

paul: deploy-bot started rollout: feature-flag reduce-prefetch canary 10% -> 50% at 09:18.

deploy-bot: rollout progress: 10% -> 35% -> 70% (09:20). No error spike on canary hosts.

raj: ran kubectl rollout restart deployment/continuous-batcher -n inference at 09:19 to pick up TTL changes on canary nodes.

olivia: customer-impact check: only small % of requests were 5xx, most were latency. CS notified customers with highest tail latencies (acme-inc, beta-shop). No data plane errors reported.

paul: metrics update at 09:22: eviction_rate down 60% on canary nodes, p95 latency trending down ~900ms. Overall requests 5xx back to baseline on canary traffic.

chen: rolling the config to 100% now, keeping the prefetch_tonic flag on. Also adding a short-lived TTL bump to avoid instant re-eviction: kv_cache.ttl_ms = 120000.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: reduce-prefetch -> 100% (09:24).

raj: removing route throttle for non-noisy customers in 5m if stability holds.

olivia: scheduling handoff — julia will take next 2h window for monitoring and postmortem prep. Note: follow-up items: add guardrails to prevent microbatch growth, auto-clamp client-requested batch hints, instrument per-customer prefetch footprint.

julia: ack — taking shift. will watch eviction_rate, microbatch_percentiles, and set an alert at eviction_rate>2x baseline to trigger auto-throttle. @sre-team FYI please keep an eye on infra memory pressure for eu-west-1.

paul: quick note for postmortem: suspected root cause = sudden traffic fan-in combined with a prefetch heuristic regression from last week's rollout that extended lookahead window. We'll assign owners.

olivia: handing off: incident remains open for 2h observation. If stable, we'll mark resolved and kick a postmortem. Thanks team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=monitoring, severity=P2, assigned=julia, followup=postmortem-assigned.
